status: P60-2 supported with a small stable carrier set
design: 5-way physical-leaf cross-fit; train entry direction on training leaves only; held-out score compares real paragraph line0->line2 against mean within-paragraph pseudo i->i+2 transitions. Page-cluster bootstrap for coordinate effects.
decision: P60-2 survives. The entry-specific effect is not diffuse: the largest stable carrier groups are k/t-family usage and near-family activation/local continuity, with shorter body-state tokens and lower entry TTR contributing secondarily. Unit inventory and total unit entropy are not stable carriers. The same sign pattern survives raw EVA, conservative composites, and the Phase56 composite representation.
interpretation: The transition is consistent with paragraph entry using a more restricted/formal token regime, followed by increased near-family activation and k/t-related morphology in the body. This is structural evidence only. The unusually large k/t contribution makes transferable entry-role testing the next direct falsification target.
next: Phase60C: pre-register held-out-section entry-vs-body prediction using token-family, k/t, prefix/suffix and slot-role features under frequency/length matching.
